Using the model
Inspect and use the model
Risk-nature history

A source reports an unfavorable effect on a delivery objective. It later declares two alternative corrections: one favorable, one mixed. A second source retains its own unfavorable report. Riskium keeps each report, source and recorded context separately. It does not choose which report is true.

Exact version	Recorded nature and pins	Relationship
A-v1	Unfavorable; context-v1, objective-v1	Original report; two recording revisions
A-v2	Favorable; context-v2, objective-v2	Explicit correction of A-v1
A-v3	Mixed; context-v1, objective-v1	Alternative correction of A-v1
B-v1	Unfavorable in another local scheme; context-v1, objective-v1	Independent documentary report; corroboration unassessed
A-v4	Favorable with later term/scheme versions	Later issue without a correction declaration; outside A-v1's correction family

Retrieving A-v1 keeps its original values after A-v2 or A-v4 exists. The correction family rooted at A-v1 contains A-v1, A-v2 and A-v3. An entry's revision chain alone does not establish a correction. These records are an authored synthetic example.

Missing information and readiness

A record without a mandatory case, nature term or source stays raw. It does not acquire an invented case identity or become an issued assertion. An issued documentary version is sealed content that passed its declared storage contract. That status does not establish that its report is true.

Context is optional in the native relation. An issued version without context is NOT_READY_CONTEXT_UNRECORDED for this retrieval task. A context without objective pins yields NOT_READY_OBJECTIVES_UNRECORDED. Both retain their actual missing values. A complete pinned context with explicit objective versions is READY_FOR_DECLARED_RETRIEVAL. This is task readiness, not factual correctness, decision approval or a risk score.

Use an exact issued version identifier to ask what it recorded. Use a case query to inspect all issued reports for that case. Use an explicit root version to inspect declared correction branches. Reproduce shows exact IDs and expected answers.

Modeling decisions
Modeling decisions
Cases, entries and scenarios

Case identity persists across descriptions, reassessments and administrative record changes. Equal text or equal scores do not automatically merge cases. A change in subject or context may require an explicit identity review.

Entries document cases. Scenario specifications describe possibilities. Occurrences refer to actual phenomena and require their own evidence. These distinctions are preserved even when one source uses a shared everyday label.

Documentary identity

An artifact, an issued version and expressed content have distinct identity roles. Issued payloads remain immutable; corrections create a new version and an explicit replacement relationship. Record time, reference time and validity time are different.

Results and comparison

A supplied score is retained as reported unless the calculation has justified inputs and a pinned method. Equal values do not authorize comparison across incompatible scales, dimensions, contexts or versions. Missing information remains unknown.

Scope
Purpose and scope

Risk knowledge often mixes the subject under analysis with its records, possible scenarios, reported results and supporting sources. Riskium makes those subjects distinct so that information can be stored, interpreted and compared under declared conditions.

A RiskCase is an identifiable subject of analysis and tracking. Several entries can record the same case, and several scenarios can concern it. An entry, a scenario specification and an actual occurrence are different entities. A description of a possible event does not establish its occurrence.

The model separates an information artifact, an issued version and its expressed content. An issued payload remains historical; a later correction does not silently replace it. Assessment information needs the method, scale, dimension, basis, context and time justified for the particular task. Recorded responsibility does not establish a mandate; administrative closure does not establish risk cessation; a reported score is not automatically reproducible computation.

Riskium models risk knowledge. It does not prescribe a complete management lifecycle, establish regulatory compliance, predict losses or
